name: renameat
synopsis: int renameat(int olddirfd, const char *oldpath, int newdirfd, const char *newpath);
description: The renameat() system call renames a file, moving it between directories if required, similar to rename(). It allows relative paths to be resolved relative to specified directory file descriptors for more flexible path handling.

parameters.name: olddirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for oldpath; AT_FDCWD for current working directory

parameters.name: oldpath
parameters.description: Path to the file or directory to rename

parameters.name: newdirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for newpath; AT_FDCWD for current working directory

parameters.name: newpath
parameters.description: New path for the file or directory

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Write or search permission is denied for the directories involved
The directory is in use and cannot be renamed
Path points outside accessible address space
Invalid pathnames, such as making a directory a subdirectory of itself
newpath is a directory but oldpath is not
A component of the path does not exist
A path component is not a directory
Operation not permitted due to permissions or sticky bit
olddirfd or newdirfd is not a valid file descriptor
olddirfd or newdirfd refers to a non-directory file
